clue.text: Ovation by order for workers' leader

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: to charge someone is to order or instruct them
a hand is a round of applause, an ovation

explanation.surface: A foreman's speech is applauded on command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ovation' leads the clue but supplies the second half: 'by' sets it beside the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargehand is a foreman who directs a small gang of workers on a site or factory floor.

clue.text: Member of eastern' church arrested when preaching

indicators.note: preaching is spoken out, so we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: copped is slang for arrested, caught by the police

explanation.surface: A churchman is taken into custody mid-sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when preaching' signals that the slang word for arrested is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A Copt is a Christian of the Coptic Church of Egypt.

clue.text: The reason why a name is mislaid

definitions.text: The reason why a name is mislaid

indicators.note: mislaid suggests the following letters are put out of their places

explanation.surface: Forgetting someone's name has a medical explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaid' rearranges A NAME IS; the whole clue also defines memory loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is memory loss, which explains forgetting what someone is called.

clue.text: Making a joke about appearance of Scottish Colonel

indicators.note: about puts the mocking word around the appearance word

parts.note: guying means making fun of someone, ridiculing
a manner is one's bearing or outward appearance

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the looks of a Highland officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Mannering is a Walter Scott novel whose hero is a colonel; 'about' wraps the mocking word round the appearance word.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Mannering appears in Walter Scott's novel, whose title gives the full name.

clue.text: Deceive gunman by eye signal

parts.note: a hood, short for hoodlum, is an armed gangster
a wink is a signal made with the eye

explanation.surface: A gunman winks to fool his victim.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink is to trick or dupe someone.

clue.text: Almost moving "Lear' in New -.York

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged name between the New York letters

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York

indicators.note: moving says the king's name must be shifted around

explanation.surface: A touring production of King Lear almost opens in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a touring Shakespeare production; 'moving' rearranges the king's name into a nobleman's title before 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means not quite, very close to.

clue.text: Whip-round — about a pound — to get powder

indicators.note: about means the turned whip goes around the pound sign
round tells us to turn the whip word the other way about

parts.note: a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
L, from the Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: Colleagues hold a collection, each chipping in a quid, to buy talcum powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' reads as a collection, but splits into Whip and 'round', which turns CAT into TAC; 'about' then puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is the soft mineral ground into talcum powder.

clue.text: Thinner sort of shirt used in singles

indicators.note: used in puts the shirt letter between the two singles

parts.note: an ace and one are both singles, a unit
a T-shirt is a kind of shirt, so T

explanation.surface: A lighter-weight shirt is worn for a tennis singles match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thinner' reads as a comparison, but it is the noun for a solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a solvent used as paint thinner and nail-varnish remover.

clue.text: Magnate makes heads roll

parts.note: capita is Latin for heads, as in per capita
a roll is a list of names

explanation.surface: A tycoon dismisses executives ruthlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads roll' suggests sackings, but CAPITA and LIST are its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitalist is a wealthy investor, a tycoon.

clue.text: Mint producing coin of the realm

parts.note: a penny is a small British coin
something of the realm belongs to the kingdom, so is royal

explanation.surface: The Royal Mint is striking a new coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like the place coins are made, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a small aromatic plant of the mint family.

clue.text: Cry for small change

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
P stands for a penny or pence, loose change

explanation.surface: Someone begs for a few coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to cry, shedding tears.

clue.text: Red-suited section of the orchestra produce deep emotions

parts.note: hearts is a red suit in cards
the strings are the violins, violas, cellos and basses

explanation.surface: Red-clad violinists move the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartstrings are one's deepest feelings, as in tugging at them.

clue.text: Huge South American mountain

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, an extra-large clothing size
SA is the abbreviation for South America

explanation.surface: A vast Andean peak is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue paints an Andean giant, but the mountain is in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is a peak in Thessaly, famous from the myth of the giants piling Pelion upon it.

clue.text: Went courting, but departed in a huff

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned phrase for a couple going steady, strolling together
to leave a meeting in protest

explanation.surface: A suitor's romance ends with a sulky exit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both an old sense of dating and leaving in protest.

clue.text: A medical speciality involving piece of catgut as styptic

indicators.note: involving means the first pieces enclose the catgut word

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine
catgut is used as string for instruments

explanation.surface: A surgical specialty uses catgut to stop bleeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A styptic stops bleeding by contracting tissue, which is what an astringent does.

clue.text: Girl, gripped by jazz, moving aimlessly

indicators.note: gripped by means the girl sits inside the jazz word

parts.note: swing is a style of jazz
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman drifts around, held in the embrace of a dance band.
explanation.definitionFit: Swanning about is idly wandering with no purpose, a British idiom.

clue.text: Hard experience in the gold trade

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to deal is to trade

explanation.surface: Life in the bullion business is tough.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful trial, a severe test of endurance.

clue.text: Panic-monger finds a mistral blowing up

indicators.note: blowing up suggests the wind's letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A scaremonger notes a fierce wind rising.
explanation.walkthrough: The mistral is a cold wind of southern France; 'blowing up' scrambles A MISTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist spreads needless fear, a scaremonger.

clue.text: Official report put on tape

definitions.meaning: the formal account, such as minutes of proceedings
to capture sound or pictures on a cassette

explanation.surface: Minutes of a meeting are captured on cassette.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a formal account; as a verb, to capture audio.

clue.text: Plant is free' from trouble without engineers,

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the easy word goes round the engineers

parts.note: comfy means at ease, free from trouble
RE stands for the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A garden is free from pests without needing engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfrey is a herbaceous plant used in herbal medicine.

clue.text: Old subjects taught thus in form

indicators.note: in places the Latin word inside the class word

parts.note: a form is a school class
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: Latin and Greek are taught in a school form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taught' just joins the definition to the wordplay; 'Old subjects' means ancient Greek and Latin studies.
explanation.definitionFit: The classics are the study of ancient Greek and Roman language and literature.

clue.text: State Gary's in!

parts.note: the state containing the steel city of Gary, near Chicago, or perhaps where a man named Gary lives

explanation.surface: Someone announces that Gary is present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' reads as a verb, say, but it is the noun: Gary is a city in this US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Gary is a steel city in this Midwest US state.

clue.text: Old geographer upsets hospital round/

indicators.note: in a down clue upsets turns the hospital word upward

parts.note: Barts is St Bartholomew's Hospital in London
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An elderly mapmaker knocks over a hospital trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: BARTS is St Bartholomew's, a London hospital; 'upsets' turns it to STRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Strabo was a Greek geographer of the first century BC.

clue.text: Make room at inn for caller

indicators.note: make tells us to construct something new from the following letters

explanation.surface: An innkeeper is asked to make space for a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' rebuilds ROOMATINN; 'caller' is one who calls a candidate forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominator names someone for office, calling them forward as a candidate.

clue.text: Travelled over to, cattle show, having nothing to lose

indicators.note: having to lose means one letter must be dropped from the show

parts.note: a rodeo is a show of cattle-roping and bronco riding
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone journeyed to a rodeo, with nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over to' is a link phrase; the comma-set 'cattle show' gives RODEO, losing one O.
explanation.definitionFit: Rode is the past tense of ride, so it means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle.

clue.text: Approach from an Italian under notice

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the Italian below the notice

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
It is short for Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: An approach is made by an Italian named in a notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; in a down entry, IT under AD gives the order.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal approach tunnel into a mine.

clue.text: Jane runs in to have a look

indicators.note: in puts the runs letter inside the look word

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Jane dashes inside to take a peek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jane' reads as just a girl, but defines the surname of Charlotte Brontë's heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre is the title heroine of Charlotte Brontë's novel.

clue.text: The consumer's wartime guarantee

parts.note: the document that promised each shopper a fixed share of scarce food during a war

explanation.surface: Shoppers in wartime were assured of their share.
explanation.definitionFit: In wartime Britain each person held a book of coupons entitling them to fixed amounts of food.

clue.text: "All is but —; renown and grace is dead" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: All is but —; renown and grace is dead" (Macbeth)

parts.words: All is but —; renown and grace is dead" (Macbeth)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: Macbeth says life is now mere trifles and playthings after Duncan's murder

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's Scottish play with a missing word.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the gap: Macbeth, after killing Duncan, says nothing in life is serious any more.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means trifles, things of no serious worth, completing the quotation.

clue.text: Stable accommodating the outsiders for a competitor

indicators.note: accommodating means the stable word holds the other letters

parts.note: constant means steady, stable

indicators.note: the outsiders of the word the are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A horse-racing yard takes in some long-shot runners for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' looks like a horse yard, but it is the adjective; 'the outsiders' gives TE, the first and last letters of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A contestant is an entrant in a contest, a rival.
